title: Predictors of effectiveness of emotion-focused transdiagnostic group therapy (ACT)
summary:
In recent years, an increasing number of people in Germany have been diagnosed with a mental disorder, such as depression or an anxiety disorder. Many affected individuals require psychotherapeutic support. Group therapies have been shown to be effective in reducing psychological symptoms and have the advantage that several people can be treated at the same time. At the same time, not all participants benefit equally from group psychotherapy. One possible reason is that participants who feel less connected to the group or feel less understood and supported by it may also benefit less from the therapy.
We aim to investigate whether individuals who experience a stronger sense of cohesion and support within the group show greater increases in well-being and greater reductions in depressive symptoms, anxiety, or stress during group therapy. In addition, we want to examine whether certain personal characteristics are associated with how much someone benefits from group therapy or whether someone terminates therapy prematurely.
The study will include 116 adults receiving treatment at the Psychotherapy Outpatient Clinic of the University of Bremen who meet criteria for a mental disorder in the area of depression, anxiety, eating disorders, and other disorders that are understood as emotional disorders. All participants will receive a structured group therapy consisting of 12 weekly sessions, each lasting 100 minutes, with a group size of approximately 8 to 10 people. The group will be led by a licensed psychological psychotherapist and a co-therapist.
Before the start of therapy, during treatment, and after completion, repeated questionnaires and diagnostic interviews will be used to assess well-being and symptoms. In addition, follow-up assessments will be conducted three and six months after the end of group therapy to examine whether changes are maintained over time. Participation is voluntary and can be discontinued at any time without disadvantage. All data will be treated confidentially and analyzed in such a way that no conclusions can be drawn about individual participants.
conditions: Bipolar affective disorder, current episode mild or moderate depression

interventions.name: Manualized ACT-based transdiagnostic group therapy (12 sessions of 100 minutes each)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients with sufficient German language skills to actively participate in group therapy will be included. The following emotional disorders will be eligible as the primary diagnosis: obsessive–compulsive disorder, panic disorder, agoraphobia, depression, generalized anxiety disorder, dysthymia, adjustment disorder, mixed anxiety and depressive disorder, social phobia (social anxiety disorder), hypochondriasis (illness anxiety), somatoform disorders, and eating disorders.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria are the presence of an acute psychotic disorder, a body mass index below 16.5, an acute bipolar disorder, a substance use disorder without verified abstinence, an autism spectrum disorder, and any other psychotherapy taking place in parallel to the group therapy. In addition, personality disorders or pronounced personality traits will be excluded if they impair the ability to participate in a group setting (in particular paranoid, schizoid, schizotypal, antisocial, histrionic, and narcissistic personality traits).
